newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto's husband indicted for murder conspiracy.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto's husband indicted for murder conspiracy.

text.p: A session court indicted former Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari on Saturday for conspiracy to murder her younger brother Murtaza Bhutto and seven companions.
Session court judge Shahnawaz Awan, conducting proceedings at Karachi Central Jail, charged 20 people, including Zardari, with conspiracy to murder Murtaza or with his actual murder.

Senior security officers, including former Deputy Inspector General of Karachi Police Shoaib Suddle, former Intelligence Bureau Chief Masood Sharif and former Senior Superintendent of Police Wajid Durrani were among those indicted for conspiracy.
Murtaza was killed along with seven companions on September 20 in Karachi by police bullets in what police said was a clash with Murtaza's guards. Bhutto was prime minister at the time.
Zardari was detained on November 5, the day President Farooq Leghari sacked Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption and misrule. He is held in Karachi Central Jail.
He told reporters on Saturday he was innocent and had been wrongly charged with conspiracy to kill his brother-in-law.
"They should carry the investigations of the case in line with the report given by the special tribunal," he said.
A report released on June 8 by a judicial tribunal described Murtaza's death as an "extra-judicial killing", which must have been sanctioned by some undisclosed "higher authority".
The tribunal rejected Bhutto's charges that Leghari had been involved in the conspiracy to kill her brother.
The next hearing of Murtaza murder case will be held on July 9.
